subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A solution has a pH of 12. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: A pH greater than 7 indicates an alkaline (basic) solution.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

questions.q: Which flame colour indicates the presence of sodium ions?
questions.explain: Sodium ions produce a yellow flame in a flame test.

questions.q: What gas is given off when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid?
questions.explain: Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen, so hydrogen gas is released.

questions.q: What is one advantage of instrumental methods such as flame emission spectroscopy?
options: They are fast, accurate and use very small samples
questions.explain: Instrumental methods like flame emission spectroscopy are fast, accurate and sensitive, working on tiny samples.

questions.q: What are the products of a neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base?
questions.explain: Acid + base → salt + water is the general neutralisation reaction.

questions.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a weak acid?
options: Strong acids fully ionise in water, weak acids only partially ionise
Weak acids have a pH above 7
questions.explain: Strength refers to the degree of ionisation: strong acids ionise completely, weak acids only partially.

questions.q: In a flame test, lithium ions give which colour?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a crimson flame.

questions.q: When a metal carbonate reacts with an acid, which gas is produced?
questions.explain: Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution such as pure water?
questions.explain: A neutral solution has a pH of exactly 7 on the 0–14 scale.

questions.q: What is produced when an acid reacts with a metal oxide?
questions.explain: A metal oxide is a base, so acid + metal oxide → salt + water.
